message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Statutes / Regulations | Practical Take‑aways | |-------|---------------------------|----------------------| | **Speed Limits** | Texas Transportation Code §§ 545.001–545.004 | • Posted limits apply; no “speed limit” exception.
• “Speed limit” is a *maximum* speed; you may drive slower. | | **Seat Belt & Child Restraint** | § 545.021 (seat belts), § 545.022 (child restraints) | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster. | | **DUI / Alcohol** | § 545.041 (driving under influence), § 545.042 (driving with a blood alcohol concentration ≥0.08%) | • Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21.
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | | **Texting & Phone Use** | § 545.051 (handheld device use) | • Handheld devices are prohibited while driving.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | § 545.061 (right‑of‑way rules) | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• Stop at stop signs and red lights. | | **School Bus** | § 545.062 (school bus rules) | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children. | | **Lane Discipline** | § 545.063 (lane discipline) | • Keep to your lane unless turning or passing. | | **Parking** | § 545.064 (parking regulations) | • No parking on sidewalks, in front of fire hydrants, or in no‑stop zones. | | **Vehicle Inspection & Registration** | § 545.065 (vehicle inspection) | • Annual inspection required for most vehicles.
• Registration renewal due annually. | | **Towing & Towage** | § 545.066 (towage) | • Towing companies must be licensed. | | **Traffic Control Devices** | § 545.067 (traffic control devices) | • Obey all traffic signals, signs, and markings. | | **Pedestrian Safety** | § 545.068 (pedestrian safety) | • Drivers must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks. | | **Emergency Vehicles** | § 545.069 (emergency vehicles) | • Pull over to the right and stop when an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches. | --- ### How to Find the Full Text 1. **Texas Transportation Code** – Available online at the Texas Legislature’s website: https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/Docs/TX/htm/TX.545.htm 2. **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)** – Offers downloadable handbooks and quick‑reference guides: https://www.dps.texas.gov/section/driver-license/driver-education 3. **Texas Motor Vehicle Commission (MVC)** – Provides registration, inspection, and licensing information: https://www.txdmv.gov/ --- ### Common Misconceptions | Myth | Reality | |------|---------| | “I can drive faster than the posted limit if I’m in a hurry.” | Speed limits are maximum speeds; exceeding them is illegal. | | “I can text while driving if I’m using a hands‑free headset.” | Handheld device use is prohibited; hands‑free is allowed. | | “If I’m under 21, I can have a BAC of 0.02%.” | Zero‑tolerance applies; any measurable alcohol is illegal. | --- ### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas - **Always keep your seat belt fastened** – it’s a legal requirement and saves lives. - **Check your mirrors and blind spots** before changing lanes or turning. - **Use your turn signals** at least 100 feet before making a turn. - **Stay alert for pedestrians** – especially in urban areas and near schools. - **Keep your vehicle in good condition** – regular inspections help avoid violations. --- #### Need More Detail? If you’re looking for specific sections of the Texas Transportation Code or want to know how a particular law applies to a situation (e.g., “What does § 545.051 say about hands‑free devices?”), let me know and I can pull up the exact statutory language for you.
